details: CONFIRMED by reading: main() line 451 calls record_event(main_dir, kind, now_stamp(), head_of(main_dir, default)); page() never prints
the head it used, so the front cannot pass it back. Landings are frequent (44 first-parent landing commits in the last 24 h on the live
repo, 6 lanes) and the front takes a turn or more between printing, writing the message in Russian, and --sent (more when the page says
"and N more" and it runs --all). Each lost window drops decisions, and the owner's 30 Oct words ask every decision to reach him once.
Size: 15 min.
evidence: lib/relay_digest.py:449-452: record_event(main_dir, kind, now_stamp(), head_of(main_dir, default))
lib/relay_digest.py:363: the header prints "since <time>" only; no head sha on the page
failing_case: Master at H1 with item X closed and decision note D on item Y unanswered since the last event. Front runs `relay digest` (page from
last..H1, shows X and D). While it writes the owner message, a lane lands H2 that closes item Z and adds decision note E on item W.
Front runs `relay digest --sent`: record_event stores head_of(...) = H2. Next `relay digest` starts at H2: Z and E appear on no page,
ever. Expected: the next page lists Z under Merged and E under Decisions, because the owner never saw them.
fix_hint: Print the head on the page ("... up to <sha8>") and make `--sent <sha>` record that sha (refuse --sent without it, naming the page's
last line as where to find it); the hook's message and the skill name `relay digest --sent <sha from the page>`.
pass_cases: 1. page printed at H1, landing H2 (closes Z, adds decision E), then --sent: the next page lists Z and E exactly once.
2. page printed at H1, nothing lands, --sent: the next page says "nothing new since <time>" (today's behaviour).
3. two `relay digest` runs with no --sent print the same page (today's behaviour, test_printing_records_nothing).
4. --sent with a head that is not an ancestor of master is refused, or falls back as resolve_start does today.
findings.summary: `relay digest --sent` stores the head at the moment it runs, not the head the page was computed on: anything that lands between printing and --sent is never shown

details: CONFIRMED: relay lands by fast-forward (the brief's own term), so master's first parent follows the branch's first-parent chain,
including its "Merge branch 'master' into wt/..." commits. Live: the last 48 h list (git log --first-parent) shows runs like
02e84019, 9d4ae8e9, 2251e6b6, 619cc9e1, 92990a4c, aeac9423, all one change. The tests build one commit per "landing", so they pass.
The setting's documented meaning ("at 5 about 4 digests a day", "15 landings") and the line the owner sees are wrong by a factor of
about 3; the digest fires that much more often, which is the noise this change exists to remove. docs/handover.md commits on master
also count (relay_inert.INERT lists it; landings() excludes only queue and checks). Size: 15 min.
evidence: digest due: 44 landings since the last digest (limit 15)
failing_case: This branch itself: `git rev-list --first-parent --count master..HEAD -- . ':(exclude).relay/queue' ':(exclude).relay/checks'` = 3
(b196c6a1, 2b59b997, caf2d44b). After `relay land` fast-forwards it, `relay digest --due` counts 3 landings for one change. Five such
changes print "digest due: 15 landings since the last digest (limit 15)". Expected: 5 landings, nothing due until the 15th change.
fix_hint: Count landings from facts that are one per landing: the "done"/landed events in <git common dir>/relay-land/events.jsonl after the last
sent event, or the items newly closed in the queue difference (changes().merged), and exclude every relay_inert.INERT path.
pass_cases: 1. one branch with 3 work commits and one "merge master" commit fast-forwarded onto master after the event: --due counts 1 landing.
2. 15 such landed branches after the event and no paid run: "digest due: 15 landings ..."; 14: nothing.
3. commits that touch only .relay/queue, .relay/checks or docs/handover.md count 0 (today's test_queue_commits_are_no_landing, plus handover).
4. a paid run ended after the event is due at any count (today's behaviour).
reason: tests/test_digest.py Due::test_a_change_of_four_commits_is_one_landing and siblings; fail at base
findings.summary: landings() counts first-parent commits, but a fast-forward landing puts every commit of the branch on master's first-parent chain, so one landing counts 3 or more

details: CONFIRMED by reading the three diffs. Brief decision: "the open question is answered a: one line per item when its decisions are
recorded, work goes on". Only SKILL.md:24-29 carries it. Global instructions win over a skill when they differ (the project's precedence),
so the contradiction resolves against the owner-reversible decision. Size: 10 min.
evidence: rules/front.md:28: in a turn an agent's or a job's end started, say nothing unless it is a question, a red default branch, a spend alert or a block only he can lift;
rules/working-with-me.md:80: say nothing unless it is a question for me, a red default branch, a spend alert or a block only I can lift
SKILL.md:28: or, once per item whose decisions were just recorded, one line with the item's title, up to three decision titles
failing_case: A notification turn after a design agent recorded 5 decision notes on item "The change cycle lands a ready change itself". Global
instructions (from rules/front.md:27-29 and rules/working-with-me.md:79-81) say: "say nothing unless it is a question, a red default
branch, a spend alert or a block only he can lift". The front skill says to send one line for that item. A front that follows the
always-loaded text (the skill loads only on demand) sends nothing; the owner sees the decisions only in the evening digest, after merge,
which is option b, not the decided a. Expected: every status text lists the per-item decision line among the exceptions.
fix_hint: Add "or one line per item whose decisions were just recorded" to the exception lists of rules/front.md and rules/working-with-me.md,
regenerate the eval system rules, extend the Texts test.
pass_cases: 1. rules/front.md contains, among the notification-turn exceptions, one line per item whose decisions were just recorded (titles, "answer by title to reverse").
2. rules/working-with-me.md says the same in the owner's voice.
3. SKILL.md keeps its exception list (unchanged).
4. test_every_status_text_limits_the_line_to_owner_requests still passes, and a new assertion finds the per-item line in all three texts.
reason: tests/test_digest.py Texts::test_every_status_text_keeps_the_per_item_decision_line_among_the_exceptions; rules/front.md and working-with-me.md carry the line; fails at base
findings.summary: the always-loaded status texts (rules/front.md, rules/working-with-me.md) forbid the per-item decision line that the front decided (7a) and the skill requires

details: CONFIRMED by reading paid_runs and listing ~/.relay/evals/relay (15 wt-* records). Rare today (paid runs go on the default branch per wave),
so LOW. Size: 5 min.
evidence: ls ~/.relay/evals/relay | grep -v master -> 15 files, e.g. 2026-10-27T14-53-11Z-wt-majority.json; records carry "branch".
failing_case: An eval run on a branch writes ~/.relay/evals/relay/<time>-wt-<branch>.json (15 such files exist, last 27 Oct). --due then prints
"digest due: a paid run ended ..." and the page's Numbers show that branch run as "last paid run". Expected: only runs on the default
branch (record field "branch") end a wave and count as the last paid run.
fix_hint: Skip records whose "branch" is not the default branch.

details: CONFIRMED by reading refusal(): key = "\n".join(lines) and the lines carry counts and dollar amounts. Correct in intent (still due), but
louder than the design's once-per-state. Size: 5 min.
evidence: digest_due.py:41 key = "\n".join(lines); relay_digest.py:411 and 417 put the count and the amount in the line.
failing_case: Digest due at 15 landings; the front was refused once and is mid-answer to the owner. A lane lands: the line becomes "16 landings", a
new key, and the next Stop is refused again; the same on every landing until --sent. The design says the hook refuses once for that state.
Expected: one refusal per reason (paid run ended at T, landing limit reached, alert of the day), not per count.
fix_hint: Key the stamp on the reason kinds plus the paid run's end time (drop the counts and amounts).
pass_cases: 1. 15 landings: refused; 16 landings without --sent: not refused again.
2. after --sent and 15 new landings: refused again (today's test).
3. a paid run ended at a new time after a refusal for landings: refused again.
findings.summary: the hook's 'once per due state' key holds the landing count and spend amount, so each new landing or spend change refuses the turn again
